note: Labeled routing cases. Labels follow SKILL.md: the cheapest reliable model; frontier only where a mistake is expensive or hard to detect; an independent review excludes the producer's vendor; the judge (jev) is never a reviewer. acceptable lists every model a careful person accepts; stakes is the label for the stakes Noul (null: not scored).
purpose: A team routes each pipeline task to one model. People act on the results.
policy: Prefer the cheapest model that does the job reliably. Spend frontier capability only where a mistake is expensive or hard to detect.

attrs.what: Check that each of 40 generated config files parses as JSON.

cases.why: A trivial check that a parser confirms: the smallest model is enough.

attrs.what: Check that the line items of 12 invoices add up to the stated totals.

cases.why: Cheap arithmetic that code can recheck: either small model.

attrs.what: Rename one function across 12 files. The build and the tests confirm the change.

cases.why: A mechanical edit that the build checks: a small or mid model, never frontier.

attrs.what: Reformat 30 internal changelog entries to the house template. An engineer reads the result before release.

cases.why: Following a template, and a person reads it: no frontier spend.

attrs.what: Read four repositories and report, with file:line citations, what the code does today.

cases.why: Bulk well-specified reading whose citations get checked: the mid tier is the sweep model. Stakes are high: SKILL.md section 5 measured 0.57, because a wrong reading of the code feeds every later step.

attrs.what: Skim 300 pages of build logs and list each distinct error code with the line where it first appears.
attrs.verifiable_by_code: partly: line numbers can be checked

cases.why: A long-context skim with checkable output: a fast or mid model.

attrs.what: Read a 900-page set of vendor contracts and extract every liability cap and termination clause. Legal signs a renewal on the result.

cases.why: A missed clause is expensive and hard to detect: a frontier long-context model.

attrs.what: Read 60 app screenshots and list every visual defect against the design spec before a public release.

cases.why: Multimodal input at release stakes: the roster's measured visual-defect model.

attrs.what: Attack a finished engineering estimate: find the underestimated item and the unpriced dependency.
attrs.needs_independence: YES - must fail differently from the producer

cases.why: A Claude estimate gets a Codex frontier review; Gemini is only an optional third lane.

attrs.what: Adversarial review of a Claude-written concurrency change in a payment service before merge.
attrs.needs_independence: YES - must fail differently from the producer

cases.why: Concurrency in payments: a measured Codex frontier reviewer, never the producer's vendor.

attrs.what: Review a Codex-written database migration for any path that loses customer data.
attrs.needs_independence: YES - must fail differently from the producer

cases.why: A Codex producer gets a Claude frontier review; data loss is expensive.

attrs.what: Check a Gemini-written summary of a design document for claims the document does not support. The team plans the next quarter on it.
attrs.needs_independence: YES - must fail differently from the producer

cases.why: A Gemini producer gets a Codex or Claude frontier check; a plan is built on it.

attrs.what: Independent check that a Claude-written unit test covers the three edge cases named in its docstring. CI runs the test. The engineer reads the check result before merge.
attrs.needs_independence: YES - must fail differently from the producer

cases.why: Independent but bounded and cheap to get wrong: a small or mid model of another vendor.

attrs.what: Write the cover letter that presents a fixed-price estimate to a customer, who will budget against it.

cases.why: Customer prose that must stay accurate: the Claude frontier model.

attrs.what: Write the customer-facing incident report on a data exposure, including exactly which data was affected.

cases.why: A wrong word here is expensive and public: the only frontier candidate.

attrs.what: Draft internal release notes from 30 merged pull request titles. An engineer edits them before they go anywhere.

cases.why: Internal prose that a person edits: errors are cheap and caught.

attrs.what: For each of 500 support tickets, give the probability that it reports a security issue. Code sends tickets above a threshold to the security team.

cases.why: A calibrated yes/no that code acts on is the judge's job; a missed report is costly. Stakes are not scored: the stakes Noul compares a frontier with a mid-tier model; a judge-only task has no single answer to it.

attrs.what: Pick one of four models for each of 30 pipeline tasks from structured attributes. Code reads the pick and the confidence. A person reviews the 30 picks before any run.

cases.why: A typed choice with a confidence for code: the judge, and the gate catches ties.

attrs.what: Score 2,000 search results for relevance to one query on five ordered levels. Code ranks the results by score.

cases.why: Many typed scores for code to rank: the judge; one bad rank is cheap and visible.

attrs.what: For each of 800 pairs of customer records, give the probability that both are the same person. Code merges pairs above a threshold.

cases.why: Calibrated yes/no probabilities that code thresholds; a wrong merge is hard to undo. Stakes are not scored: the stakes Noul compares a frontier with a mid-tier model; a judge-only task has no single answer to it.
